42387196.title: Automatic lesion segmentation in ⁶⁸Ga-PSMA PET/CT and ¹⁷⁷Lu-PSMA SPECT/CT: added value of PET-guided SPECT in a bicentric study.

42474504.title: Smoking reshapes systemic metabolic coordination across lung cancer subtypes: a multicenter total-body 18F-FDG PET/CT study with tumor habitat imaging.

42481881.title: Preclinical PET characterization of [68Ga]Ga-EMP-100 for non-invasive assessment of c-Met in NSCLC.

41499307.title: Prognostic Implications of Volume-based Quantitative 18F-FDG PET/CT Biomarkers in Pulmonary Sarcoidosis.

41553532.title: Comparative evaluation of [68Ga]Ga-FAP-2286 and [18F]FDG PET/CT in breast cancer and initial experience with [177Lu]Lu-FAP-2286 therapy.

41748296.title: Quantitative PSMA PET Biomarkers for Predicting Response to 177Lu-PSMA Therapy in Prostate Cancer: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.

41290365.title: The Role of Amyloid-β and Tau PET in the New Era of Alzheimer Disease Therapies.

41559331.title: PET imaging of alpha-synuclein: from radiotracer design through in vitro and in vivo translation.

41631935.title: The PRIMARY Scoring System on PSMA PET for Clinically Significant Prostate Cancer Detection: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

41365508.title: FAPI PET in the Diagnosis and Management of Inflammatory Diseases: Clinical Value and Future Perspectives.

41622307.title: Bridging the gaps in fibroblast activation protein targeted radionuclide therapy: a translational perspective.

41455672.title: Current status of FAP therapy in solid tumors.

41946604.title: The value of [18F]FDG PET/CT in fever of unknown origin (FUO): an update and future aspects.

42014234.title: New targets for PET imaging of inflammation.

41926960.title: [177Lu]-PSMA-617-PSMA-617 in oligometastatic hormone sensitive prostate cancer (BULLSEYE): an open-label, randomised, phase 2 study.

42080884.title: Multicentre validation of the PRECISE scoring system for prostate MRI during active surveillance.

Clinical relevance PSA-density cut-offs of 0.20 (PI-RADS 1-2) and 0.12 ng/mL² (PI-RADS 3) can guide biopsy decisions. In PI-RADS 1-3 patients with large prostate (≥ 60 mL), PSA-density becomes significantly less predictive, and low values may not reliably exclude csPCa.

41556856.title: Utility of Serum Biomarkers in Addition to Ultrasound for Early Detection of Hepatocellular Carcinoma in High-Risk Patients: A Randomized Controlled Trial.

41609770.title: MRI to guide clinical management of rectal cancer: updated consensus recommendations from the European Society of Gastrointestinal and Abdominal Radiology (ESGAR)-PART I primary staging.

40498155.title: Targeted alpha therapy: a comprehensive analysis of the biological effects from "local-regional-systemic" dimensions.

41188529.title: Critical review of partial volume correction methods in PET and SPECT imaging: benefits, pitfalls, challenges, and future outlook.

39316095.title: Updated practice guideline for dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA).

39387894.title: EANM/SNMMI guideline/procedure standard for [18F]FDG hybrid PET use in infection and inflammation in adults v2.0.

39891713.title: Radiotheranostic landscape: A review of clinical and preclinical development.

40887378.title: Implementation of Radiotheranostics: Challenges, Barriers, and IAEA-Driven Strategies for Sustainable Access.

40404395.title: Rethinking Dosimetry: A European Perspective.

Although external-beam radiotherapy has long integrated dosimetry into standard practice, RPT historically relied on fixed radiopharmaceutical activities and absorbed dose-effect relationships adapted from external-beam radiotherapy, often without accounting for the unique pharmacokinetics, absorbed dose rate dynamics, and biologic responses of systemically administered radiopharmaceuticals.

38971533.title: Low-to-moderate alcohol consumption is associated with increased fibrosis in individuals with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease.

extras.text: Metabolic risk factors such as overweight, diabetes or dyslipidemia, and alcohol consumption can cause liver disease. extras.label: Impact and implications

Additionally, as most patients with MASLD are seen in primary care instead of specialist settings, cost and availability of the tests should be taken into consideration. In this multicentre study, the use of the Fibrosis-4 index followed by liver stiffness measurement by vibration-controlled transient elastography effectively identified patients who would later develop liver-related events. 41047080.title: Prognostic value of liver stiffness measurement vs. biochemical response in primary biliary cholangitis.
41047080.authors: Wong YJ, Lam L, Soret PA, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusions
conclusion.text: Discordance between LSM and biochemical response is frequent. Most recent or current LSM is the strongest predictor of first liver-related events in patients with PBC, irrespective of prior biochemical response or LSM trajectory.

extras.label: Impact and implications
extras.text: Both liver stiffness measurement (LSM) and biochemical response have prognostic significance in patients with primary biliary cholangitis. However, the clinical relevance and how discordant biochemical and LSM changes should be best interpreted remain unclear. In this large international multicenter study, we demonstrated that once the current LSM is known, prior LSM trajectories and biochemical changes did not improve the prediction of liver-related events in patients with primary biliary cholangitis. Our finding addresses a common clinical dilemma in risk-stratifying PBC patients with discordant biochemical and LSM responses. Importantly, the use of the latest LSM value for risk prediction significantly simplifies the use of LSM in clinical decision-making for PBC patients with multiple LSM readings.
